description:
Team RAVYN bridges aerospace systems engineering and interactive game design. We are building an immersive web-based simulator where players manage real-world mission trade-offs—balancing payload mass, power budgets, delta-V, and launch costs from concept to launch.

We bring together game architecture, full-stack development, orbital physics, and UI/UX design to deliver a prototype powered by real telemetry and dynamic simulation mechanics that makes mission planning intuitive.
summary:
RAVYN MISSION LAB is an award-contending 2.5D retro systems-engineering RPG inspired by the visual aesthetic of Pokémon White 2. Players step into the shoes of a Rookie Systems Engineer at a NASA-inspired facility, guiding a spacecraft across an immersive 4-Act Campaign that covers all four official NASA mission segments and transitions through JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4).

The game combines vibrant pixel-art top-down exploration with high-stakes, physics-driven mini-games, replacing dry text dialogues with tactile engineering challenges.
details:
RAVYN MISSION LAB is an educational 2.5D retro pixel-art RPG (inspired by Pokémon White 2) built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

  • What it does: Players step into the shoes of a Rookie Systems Engineer, guiding a spacecraft across a 4-Act Campaign that covers all four NASA mission segments and JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4)—featuring cryogenic LOX venting, Max-Q throttling, zero-G satellite detumbling, DSN Doppler waveform locking, and spectrometer data filtering.
  • Benefits & Impact: Turns complex aerospace engineering and GMAT orbital mechanics into tactile, fast-paced arcade mini-games, making space systems design accessible and engaging for students and the public.
  • Tech Stack: 100% self-contained single-file HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, ES6+ JavaScript, and a procedural WebAudio synth (built with Gemini & ChatGPT assistance; designed by Team RAVYN).
  • Why it's creative: Fuses nostalgic pixel-art RPG exploration with rigorous, physics-driven aerospace constraints where early choices (like fuel efficiency and signal lock) directly impact later mission outcomes.
